samples.claim: entry_size<T> checks TypeId under read lock, recovers poisoned guards with into_inner, then conditionally writes entry.or_insert(contextual accessor). samples.claim: Timestamp encoding is timestamp:unit:timezone; absent timezone uses -, present timezone text is verbatim. Duration uses duration:unit; Struct uses struct. Dictionary first converts value and index types, constructs dict:value:index:false, then immediately parses the result back through DataType::try_from. Failure becomes Error::schema explaining the type/string does not parse back, preventing a later Field::data_type unwrap on strings that embed unrepresentable colon-separated components or child-dependent types. The check is parse success, not exact Arrow identity (views normalize). List/LargeList distinguish a Struct element with .struct suffix; they do not inline the child logical type. View normalization is explicit at rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:337-340.

samples.claim: validate first rejects dots and duplicates among top-level names. It collects reserved negative lineage IDs only from top-level fields whose name maps to that same ID, then pre-order checks every ID: negative IDs outside that allowed set fail, and every duplicate fails. A nested reuse of an allowed reserved ID eventually fails duplication against its top-level owner. It does not check lineage datatype/nullability, parent_id consistency or nested name uniqueness. Every field's reconstructed DataType is passed to fixed-size-list dimension validation; malformed Field::data_type may panic before returning a validation error. Primary-key verification is a separate call, not part of validate.
samples.review_note: Matches top-level name/ID checks and fixed-list validation; no parent/type/nullability validation or primary-key call in body.

samples.claim: push accepts one Option<u16> per old physical row. For Some, reject out-of-range label and checked per-destination u32 increment overflow before advancing any physical counters; None only advances physical counters. total_rows increments as ordinary u64. When rows_in_block reaches block_rows, append a full snapshot of all running counters and reset rows_in_block to zero. A destination can hold at most u32::MAX rows, whose last zero-based offset is u32::MAX-1; this builder cannot represent count2^32.
samples.review_note: Matches checked destination increment before physical counters and full-block flush; count2^32 unavailable.

samples.claim: log_2_ceil(val:u32)->u32 always asserts val>0. It selects the most significant nonzero byte via val>>16 and subsequent >>8 branches, returning the lookup width plus 0/8/16/24. The result is floor(log2(val))+1 for positive val, not mathematical ceil(log2(val)) at powers of two (e.g. 256 yields nine). Documentation examples follow this bit-width behavior. Two branch comments mislabel the tested byte ranges: the upper_half==0/third_quarter!=0 branch uses bits 8..16, and upper_half!=0/first_quarter==0 uses bits 16..24; the code shifts/offsets are authoritative.
samples.review_note: Matches branch offsets, bit-width output and mislabeled source comments; full256-entry table reread.
